A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRASS/FACTGRASS research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution-accuracy and compression-time experiments, Llama throughput measurements, and a qualitative attribution example in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results in Section 4, including revised MAESTRO measurements, throughput comparisons, and qualitative attribution results.

M1.justification: The masking objective, sparsification followed by SJLT, and FACTGRASS's factorized sparsification/reconstruction/projection procedure remain unchanged. Expanded layer-specific notation and diagrams do not establish a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, CIFAR2, MAESTRO, WikiText, and the billion-token OpenWebText subset, alongside the same synthetic projection benchmark. No dataset, task, or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained within corresponding experiments: Gaussian and FJLT projections, masking/SJLT variants, and LOGRA. Newly discussed training-dynamics methods are cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: For MAESTRO, Table 1(c) changes GRASS's intermediate mask size from 64k_max to 4k_max, while Appendix B.2 changes the TRAK ensemble from 10 to 5 independently trained checkpoints. Other datasets, splits, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged. These reported revisions do not establish whether experiments were rerun or documentation was corrected.

E4.justification: Table 1(c) revises the existing comparison of masking alone, SJLT alone, and their combination under a smaller intermediate mask, changing evidence about the components' accuracy/cost tradeoff. The MNIST ablation, synthetic sparsity analysis, and Llama case study remain unchanged; no new robustness study is added.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 revises the reported independently trained checkpoint counts from 10 for all three TRAK benchmarks to 10, 10, and 5 for MNIST, CIFAR2, and MAESTRO respectively. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice appears.

E6.justification: Table 1(c) substantially revises the music-generation comparison. At k=8192, Selective Mask LDS changes from 0.1586 to 0.3733, reversing its ranking against GRASS with Selective Mask, whose LDS changes from 0.3390 to 0.3657. GRASS with Random Mask time changes from 2.7202 to 0.7433 seconds. These are revised-setting results, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Tables 1(a,b,d), Table 2, and the projection benchmark retain their results.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2 restates existing complexity bounds after redefining dimensions rather than supplying a new guarantee. However, newly added layer-wise iFVP equations in Section 3.3.2 multiply by F and its compressed counterpart without inversion, creating a mathematical inconsistency with the retained inverse-FIM definition in Section 2.1.

C1.justification: The central claims remain sparse gradient compression, a factorized linear-layer variant, competitive attribution quality, and up to 165% faster billion-scale compression throughput. The broader title and rewritten complexity notation reframe claims already present rather than introduce a new central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 changes the explanation of dense Gaussian runtime from dependence on nonzero entries to failure to exploit input sparsity. The conclusion removes the explicit statement that explaining Random Mask's effectiveness theoretically remains open. Existing LDS, projection/preconditioning, and qualitative-outlier caveats remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a separate repository link for the SJLT CUDA kernel in Section 3.1; the main GRASS repository link is retained. It also removes the conflicting 40 GB memory statement from the Gaussian-baseline footnote while retaining the documented 48 GB A40 setup.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and A.1 expand positioning through a data-attribution survey and discussion of TracIn, SGD-Influence, and Data Value Embedding. This extends connections to training-dynamics methods while retaining the existing sketching, K-FAC, LiSSA, and DataInf discussion.

P1.justification: Section 3.3.2 receives substantial explanatory rewriting, with explicit layer-specific dimensions and clearer differentiation of intermediate and final compression sizes. Appendix A.1 is reorganized, notation is revised throughout, and the title, introductory explanations, and section formatting change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the dense/sparse projection illustrations and adds diagrams for masking, GRASS, LOGRA, and FACTGRASS, plus an unnumbered complexity-comparison table. The existing projection benchmark and qualitative example are retained as Figures 4 and 9. These additions substantially change how the method is visually explained.

improvement.justification: The new diagrams, complexity summary, and clearer layer-specific explanation make the existing algorithms easier to follow, while the separate SJLT link improves code access. These gains are tempered by the newly inconsistent iFVP equations and removal of the random-mask theoretical caveat. The revised MAESTRO scores use changed settings and therefore do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
